q: Predrag Djordjevic and Stelios Giannakopoulos arrived at Olympiacos together in 1996 from the same Greek club. Which one?
hint: Dusan Bajevic signed both Djordjevic and Giannakopoulos from Paniliakos in 1996, and both went on to win every title of the seven-year run.

q: Olympiacos led 1-0 at Anfield in December 2004 through a curling free-kick, before Liverpool won 3-1 with a late Steven Gerrard strike. Who scored that free-kick?
hint: Rivaldo bent the free-kick into the Kop end to put Olympiacos ahead on 8 December 2004, before Sinama Pongolle, Mellor and Gerrard turned the group tie around and sent Liverpool on their way to Istanbul.

q: Olympiacos' seven-in-a-row ended when they were beaten to the 2003-04 title. Which club took it?
hint: Panathinaikos won the 2003-04 championship, ending Olympiacos' seven consecutive titles from 1996-97 to 2002-03.

q: Predrag Djordjevic played 13 seasons at Olympiacos between 1996 and 2009. How many Greek championships did he collect?
hint: Twelve, from thirteen attempts. Olympiacos won the title every season Djordjevic was there apart from 2003-04, when their Athens rivals pipped them by two points.

q: Olympiacos signed the Brazilian playmaker Giovanni in the summer of 1999. Which club did they buy him from?
hint: Giovanni joined Olympiacos from Barcelona in 1999, three years after the Catalans had signed him from Santos.

q: Olympiacos demolished and rebuilt Karaiskakis Stadium in just 14 months, moving into the new ground in which year?
hint: The rebuilt Karaiskakis Stadium opened in 2004, in time to stage football at the Athens Olympics; Olympiacos' first competitive match there was a 2-1 win over Kallithea on 19 September 2004.

q: Stelios Giannakopoulos won the Greek championship in all seven of his seasons at Olympiacos, from 1996-97 to 2002-03, then left in May 2003 for which Premier League club?
hint: Sam Allardyce signed him on 28 May 2003, a year before he won Euro 2004 with Greece, and he stayed at the Reebok until he was released in 2008.

q: Olympiacos signed a Brazilian Ballon d'Or winner in July 2004. Which club did they buy him from?
hint: He joined Olympiacos on 22 July 2004 from Cruzeiro, where he had spent only around two months after leaving AC Milan.

q: In February 1981, 21 fans were crushed to death leaving Karaiskakis Stadium after a 6-0 Olympiacos win. Which gate gave the tragedy its name?
hint: The crush on 8 February 1981 happened at Gate 7, where a half-closed exit door trapped fans rushing out to celebrate. Olympiacos' main supporters' association still carries the name Gate 7 in memory of the 21 who died.

q: Before taking charge at Olympiacos in 1996, Dusan Bajevic had already won four Greek championships as manager of which club?
hint: Bajevic won four league titles at AEK Athens between 1989 and 1994 before crossing to Olympiacos, where he won three more in a row and later added the 2004-05 championship.

q: Olympiacos won the 2024 UEFA Europa Conference League final 1-0 against Fiorentina with a header in the 116th minute. Who scored it?
hint: Ayoub El Kaabi headed in Santiago Hezze's cross in the 116th minute at the Agia Sophia Stadium in Athens, making Olympiacos the first Greek club to win a European trophy.

q: Olympiacos reached the Champions League quarter-finals in 1998-99, losing 2-1 away and drawing 1-1 at home to go out 3-2 on aggregate. Which club knocked them out?
hint: Juventus won the Turin leg 2-1 through Inzaghi and Conte, and a 1-1 draw in Athens was enough to see them through 3-2. They went out themselves in the semi-final, beaten 4-3 on aggregate by Manchester United.

q: Giovanni spent six seasons at Olympiacos, from 1999 until 2005. How many Greek league titles did he win there?
hint: Giovanni won five championships with Olympiacos — 1999-2000, 2000-01, 2001-02, 2002-03 and 2004-05 — missing out only in 2003-04, the season he finished as the league's top scorer with 21 goals.
